title: One-Handed Blades in Phantom Blade Zero - All 10 and Where Each One Is
description: All ten one-handed blades in Phantom Blade Zero in one table: where each one is found, the six that publish a combat property, the two attached to bells, and the single Tempering branch that turns the starter blade into Infernal Rouge.
keyword: phantom blade zero one handed weapons

sections.title: The Largest of the Three Blade Families
sections.content:
Ten of the 26 blades in Phantom Blade Zero that have a recorded acquisition point are classed one-handed. That makes this the largest family, ahead of dual-wield and two-handed, which sit at eight each. The official roster is bigger than any of these figures: S-GAME's August 2026 deep dive put the shipped count at more than 30 main weapons, so the ten here are the ones published sources tie to a place, not the whole set.

A one-handed blade occupies one of the two Primary slots. Soul carries two primary blades and two secondary Phantom Edges at once, and switching between the two primaries refunds stamina immediately, which is why the loadout rewards carrying a blade you would not otherwise main. Everything on this page is about that first slot; the full blade index covers all 26 across the three classes, and the weapons hub covers the system and the Phantom Edges.

The ten are worth reading together rather than one at a time, because the pattern is in the spread: two are handed to you by the story, two are tied to bells, four sit in the open world, one is a boss drop and one only exists as a Tempering result. No two of them are obtained the same way twice in a row.

sections.content:

Two notes on the table. Freezing Chaos is recorded at the Threadbound Great Tree in Crimson Forest, but one checklist attributes it to Yucong instead; the page for it carries the discrepancy rather than picking a side. Wild Oriole Sword is listed as Mu Xiaokui's blade in the Puppet Testing Grounds, which reads more like who was carrying it than where it lies.

sections.title: Why Two of the Ten Hang Off a Bell
sections.content:
Jagged Steel and Tianxuan Bronze Sword are the only two one-handed blades attached to a bell rather than to a boss, a chest or a story beat. That looks like a quirk of these two until you check the rest of the wiki: bells turn up in eleven separate location records, and they are not only where weapons sit.

  • Weeping Creek Valley — Rustblade Pavilion bell: Jagged Steel, and the fight against Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute.
  • Village of Lu — The Lady Grounds bell: Tianxuan Bronze Sword.
  • Weeping Creek Valley — First Meeting with Yu'er bell: the dual-wield blade Sanguine Twin.
  • Mount Soulrend — Giant's Lair bell: the two-handed Bonesaw.
  • Elsewhere — Terrace bell, South Gate bridge bell, Statue Grounds bell, The Singing Pond bell, Whiteshadow's Fall bell, Back Street Archway bell: each anchors a named encounter rather than a pickup.

So a bell in this game functions as a map pin, not a reward type. The practical version: when a region gives you a bell, it is telling you that something named is nearby, and that something may be a weapon, a mini-boss or both. Three of the game's recorded weapons and at least six named fights are keyed to one. Walking a region bell by bell covers more of the record than walking it boss by boss, because several pickups have no fight attached at all.

The Rustblade Pavilion case is worth spelling out, since it is the one place two records overlap. The weapon Jagged Steel is recorded at that bell, and the encounter page for the boss of the same name puts its fight at the same bell. The weapon page does not state that the boss drops it, so this page does not either; it only points out that the two records agree on the place, which is enough to make that bell worth a detour even if you skipped the fight.

sections.title: Six Publish a Property, Four Do Not
sections.content:
Six of the ten carry a property that a published source actually states. The other four carry nothing, and that is a finding rather than an oversight: Phantom Blade Zero does not print a numeric stat sheet for individual weapons, so a property only appears in this wiki when a source named one. Freezing Chaos, Wild Oriole Sword and Wooden Sanguine have no recorded effect of any kind beyond existing, and Sanguine's only printed trait is the Tempering route it opens.

What you needThe one that states it
Sustained damage on a target that survives a comboJagged Steel — slashes cause Bleeding
To break a guard or shield rather than chip itTianxuan Bronze Sword — high shield-break
To deal with projectiles and threadsSoft Snake Sword — deflects attacks, cuts threads
A ranged option without giving up the primary slotThe Fanatic's Broken Blade — drinking lets the blade be thrown
A boss's own move in your handsAureate — mimics Zuo Shang's Golden Sword Energy
A safety net on a lethal hitInfernal Rouge — Bloodline Rebirth

Read that table as a lookup, not a ranking. Nothing published compares the numbers behind these effects, so the honest ordering is by what problem each one solves. If two of them solve the same problem for you, the wiki has no basis for telling you which wins.

It also means the four without a stated property are not 'secret' or 'hidden' — there is no undiscovered effect waiting at a higher upgrade level. Upgrading raises attack and poise-break and can add a move at certain thresholds, but it does not reveal a trait that no source ever mentioned.

sections.title: The Only One-Handed Tempering Branch
sections.content:
Exactly one of the ten is a Tempering result: Infernal Rouge, made from Sanguine at upgrade level 5. The whole chain is two steps long and it starts in your hands at the beginning of the game.

  • Sanguine — story reward, the starting blade. Its printed trait is that it Tempers into Infernal Rouge at level 5.
  • Infernal Rouge — reached by taking Sanguine to level 5. Arrives with Bloodline Rebirth, which heals to full and boosts attack when a hit would have been lethal.

The reason this matters more than it looks: Tempering converts one blade into another and keeps the upgrade level. You are not spending thirty levels on a starter weapon and then throwing them away — the investment carries into the result. That is what stops Sanguine from being the disposable opening item it resembles.

It is also the only branch in the one-handed class. The two-handed class has its own pair, Sanguine Reach into Blazing Edge by way of Scorched Flame shards, and the weapons hub carries the full tree. Nothing else in the one-handed list upgrades sideways into another named blade.

One caveat worth stating: levelling Sanguine to 5 is a real cost, and the return is one blade with one revival trait. If you are going to run a one-handed primary anyway, it is close to free. If you are not, this is not a reason to switch.

sections.title: Choosing Between Them Without a Stat Sheet
sections.content:
With no damage numbers to compare, the usable decision inputs are route, property and the second Primary slot. Three workable shapes:

  • Carry the starter and let it mature. Sanguine into Infernal Rouge costs nothing extra if you were going to upgrade a blade regardless, and Bloodline Rebirth covers the one mistake that ends a run. Pair it with a property blade in the other slot so the safety net is not also your only damage source.
  • Pick the property that matches the wall you are stuck on. A boss that turtles behind a guard is a shield-break problem, which is Tianxuan Bronze Sword. A boss that outlasts your combo is a Bleeding problem, which is Jagged Steel. A fight full of projectiles or hanging threads is Soft Snake Sword. This is the only comparison the published record actually supports.
  • Take the earliest reachable one and stop looking. Five of the ten are in the first three regions, two of them on bells, so a one-handed run does not need to wait for a boss drop to be functional. Aureate is the only one of the ten locked behind a named kill.

What the record cannot tell you is which of the ten is strongest, and any page that claims otherwise is inventing the number. What it can tell you is that the class is well covered early, that only one entry is a boss drop, and that a single Tempering chain runs through it.

sections.title: Source Status
sections.content: This is a tier-2 page: it aggregates the one-handed entries generated from src/data/entities/weapons.json and stays in step with the ten individual blade pages. Acquisition points, classes and published properties come from those entries; nothing here is estimated. Where a source conflicts with another — Freezing Chaos's location, Shadowless Edge's Tempering route — the conflict is stated rather than resolved. Damage, scaling and speed are absent across the whole site because the game does not expose them per weapon.
